newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Treasury posts Sept deficit of 408 mln.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Treasury posts Sept deficit of 408 mln.

text.p: Brazil's Treasury posted a 408 million real deficit according to the cash concept in the month of September, bringing the deficit for the year to 5.372 billion reais, the National Treasury said in a statement.
It said receipts totalled 7.34 billion reais and expenditures were 7.748 billion reais.
The Treasury posted a 430 million real surplus in August.
September's primary result was a 711 million real surplus and the operational deficit for the month came in at 739 million reais, the statement said.

The Treasury said its operational deficit for the first nine months of the year represented 0.75 percent of gross domestic product versus a deficit of 1.04 percent of GDP in the same period a year ago.
Real interest payments on Treasury obligations totalled 1.45 billion reais in September versus 1.597 billion reais in August and 1.91 billion reais in September 1995, it said.
The Treasury added that of all ordinary expenditures, 56 percent, or 2.778 billion reais, was spent on payroll and social security payments.

The Treasury also spent a little more than 111 million reais on external debt obligations, with 45.25 million reais going to international organizations, 28.15 million reais going for Brazil Invest Bond (BIB), 16.5 million reais to the Paris Club of creditor nations and 7.7 million reais on Brazil's sovereign samurai bond. Brazil also paid 13.54 million reais to private banks and governmental agencies.
